title: Dating the record and the collector who broke old records
summary: Handy and his cousin argued over the date printed on the record; a clarinetist friend who collected old records had thrown some away.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now how did you know the date the record was made?
No, I didn't write it down, but we used to argue about it so much.
My cousin and I, he'd want to say it was made in one year and I'd say it was made in another, we'd run back home and get the record. Look on it.
And it had it written on the record?
Yeah, it was on there. And it had the date on there.
Well, we'll try to find it.
I don't know where you're going to find it.
Oh, I know a guy who collects those things, right? Oh, yeah. The clarinet player? Yeah, yeah.
He collects those old records like that.
Well, he might find it then. Matter of fact, I think those old men broke up a lot of old records he had about five, six years ago. Mm. Just threw them out of the yard, broke them all up.
That's terrible. Mm-hmm. Shouldn't do that when things are worth money.

Well, I didn't know those wastes and things. No, he didn't know those wastes. He just got tired of laying around there in the way. He just threw them out of the yard and broke them up. Had about 12, 15 of them he threw out there. Trash. After he joined church, he don't worry what does no more. So, sit down and look at television. That's his biggest, I don't know, sit down after he come awake and look at television and sleep.
